patterns.failure: An earlier result is reopened using newly edited inputs or configuration, so the displayed candidate no longer belongs to the work that produced it.
patterns.counterexample: Start with input A, obtain a result, edit the current input to B, then open the result from A.
patterns.control: Keep an immutable input and configuration identity with each result, or explicitly invalidate it after edits. Check reopening an earlier result after changing the current input.
patterns.notApplicable: No results survive input changes and the product has no delayed result, retained candidate or result-to-editor handoff.
patterns.evidence: RC6 and RC7 product assessments exposed result-handoff identity failures. These concrete failures support this pattern; they do not establish a general benefit from the registry.

patterns.failure: Repeated easy symbol patterns exercise similar branching and pruning, concealing the cost of other valid workload families.
patterns.counterexample: A fast local witness passes while an independently generated valid witness with a different branching or pruning pattern fails the same completion target.
patterns.control: Generate an independent valid witness that stresses another cost driver. Measure correct, complete results on that workload early; profile a missed target and correct the costly work without reducing the workload or target.
patterns.notApplicable: The changed operation has no constraint search or input-dependent branching or pruning cost.
patterns.evidence: RC7 recorded a local median completion of 4.515 seconds while six external cases reached 120-second timeouts. This contrast supports checking distinct workload families; it does not prove a general benefit from the registry.

patterns.failure: Reading method instructions is treated as activating the method, and product results are attributed to a method run without its native runtime phases or gate evidence.
patterns.counterexample: An evaluation reports method-guided implementation after an instruction read, but cannot identify an approved scope, a native Dev phase or the corresponding gate evidence.
patterns.control: The coordinator checks approved scope and the native phase before Dev work, then checks actual gate evidence before method assessment. Canonical scripts/aim_evaluation_guard.py is a repository-only evaluation harness, not an installed-skill command.
patterns.notApplicable: The activity is not assessing whether a product result was produced by an activated AIM workflow.
patterns.evidence: RC6 evaluation exposed the gap between instruction reading and workflow activation. The canonical repository guard supplies a bounded evaluation check; this provenance does not establish a general benefit from the registry.
